fix_commit.message: avformat/mpegts: bounds-check JPEG-XS header_size before padding
fix_commit.author: Ruikai Peng

findings.title: Unvalidated JPEG-XS header_size used to advance/shrink packet buffer before padding memset
findings.message: In new_pes_packet(), when a JPEG-XS elementary stream PES payload is detected (stream_id == 0xbd, stream_type == 0x32, and the 'jxes' marker present), the code reads a 32-bit header_size value directly from the untrusted packet payload (AV_RB32(pkt->data)) and immediately uses it to advance pkt->data and shrink pkt->size (pkt->data += header_size; pkt->size -= header_size;) with no validation that header_size <= pkt->size. Because header_size is attacker-controlled (read straight from the transport stream payload), a crafted packet can set header_size to a value larger than pkt->size (e.g. 0xFFFFFF00). This causes pkt->size to underflow to a huge value (since pkt->size is a signed int this becomes a large negative/garbage value depending on representation) and pkt->data to point past the end of the allocated buffer. Immediately after, the code executes `memset(pkt->data + pkt->size, 0, AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE);` which computes an out-of-bounds address and writes AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE zero bytes there, resulting in an out-of-bounds heap write / memory corruption that can crash the process or potentially be leveraged for further exploitation.
findings.suggestion: Validate that header_size does not exceed pkt->size before advancing/shrinking the packet buffer. If header_size > pkt->size, mark the packet as corrupt and return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA instead of proceeding to adjust pkt->data/pkt->size and performing the trailing memset padding.

ground_truth.root_cause: Missing bounds validation of an attacker-controlled length field (header_size) read from network/file input before it is used in pointer arithmetic that adjusts a buffer's base pointer and size, which are later used to compute a memset destination address.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Unvalidated JPEG-XS header_size used to advance/shrink packet buffer before padding memset
